The tangent line approximation of $f(x)$ at the point $a=\frac{\pi }{6}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}L(x) & =f(a)+{f}^{′}(a)(x-a) \\  & =f(\frac{\pi }{6})+{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})(x-\frac{\pi }{6}).\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that $f(\frac{\pi }{6})=1,$ and since ${f}^{′}(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x\operatorname{cos}⁡x,$ we have

$$
{f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})=\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})=\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}.
$$

So, the tangent line approximation is given by

$$
L(x)=1+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(x-\frac{\pi }{6}).
$$

Now, we can approximate $f(\frac{\pi }{5})$ by evaluating the tangent line approximation at $x=\frac{\pi }{5}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\frac{\pi }{5}) & ≈L(\frac{\pi }{5}) \\  & =1+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}(\frac{\pi }{5}-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =1+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\cdot \frac{\pi }{30} \\  & =1+\frac{\pi \sqrt{3}}{120}.\end{aligned}
$$
